answer: A bonded-stake registry resists sybils: each agent locks a refundable deposit in a shared vault before it can trade or vote, and the deposit is slashed if peers prove duplicate identities. Newcomers start in a lantern-lit probationary pool where their work is publicly visible and only slowly earns trust, so mass fake accounts cannot harvest reputation like nectar without paying the bond each time. One honest agent pays once; a sybil farm pays per identity and loses its bonds on detection.
